title: Review: jmap-client convergence check round 9
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two real issue-generators: (1) the TLS trust store inconsistency between reqwest and tungstenite will cause 'works for HTTP, fails for WebSocket' reports; (2) the test_fetch_session_rejects_non_http_other_urls mock reuse bug means downloadUrl and eventSourceUrl rejection is untested. The auth.rs doc error about silent drops will mislead AuthProvider implementors.
Confidence: 85% chance of no missed P0 bug. Least confident flags: JMAP-3m6.5 (wiremock mock ordering) — this is verifiable but I did not run a targeted test to confirm the mock-reuse behavior. Uncertainty driven by: not having run targeted experiments on wiremock ordering in this loop pattern; not having read full reqwest TLS feature matrix. Would raise confidence if: add explicit test for downloadUrl rejection with isolated mock scope; verify wiremock ordering with a test that fails if ordering is wrong.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The code is structurally sound (#![forbid(unsafe_code)], #[non_exhaustive] on error and public enums, thiserror, proper guard clauses). Two real API design issues: AuthProvider returns owned String forcing a clone-per-request (JMAP-3m6.14), and error variants wrap String instead of structured types losing serde_json position/kind info (JMAP-3m6.15). Missing Clone on transport/auth structs (JMAP-3m6.17) is a real usability gap. Two clippy-level findings (.to_string() on literals, Self:: vs path). No unsafe, no gratuitous clones outside the trait-mandated one, no unwrap in production code (the one .expect in client.rs is provably correct with comment).
Rust idiom confidence: 88% chance of no missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-3m6.14 (Cow return type) — changing the AuthProvider trait signature is a semver break and may be intentionally deferred; JMAP-3m6.15 (structured error types) — adding serde_json::Error variant creates a semver dep on serde_json in the error enum (which is already a dep, but now callers must match it). Uncertainty driven by: not having checked whether jmap-types Invocation/JmapResponse derive Eq (which would affect WsFrame); not having verified whether serde_json::Value::Eq is actually implemented (assumed from docs). Both are verifiable with a compile check.
